Prior art is console.group/groupEnd nesting in core/new/1/Page.class.js + Router.js (legacy, read-only) — and its own doc warns an unclosed console.groupCollapsed() on a thrown render() nests every later log line forever. Reused the lesson, not the code: Logger.group()'s close() runs in a try/finally-equivalent (catch + rethrow) so a throw inside a group still closes it.

decision.question: what IS the Logger's core data store
options: a flat array of {t,depth,args} and derive nesting from depth on render
a nested tree (group entries hold their own child array), Memory output = that tree
decision.chose: nested tree; Logger.Memory owns logger.entries and is attached by the constructor (not truly opt-in, despite the brief listing it beside Console/JSONL) because LogView has to walk parent->child to render groups as nested <details>, and re-deriving a tree from a flat depth-tagged list on every render is more code for no benefit
decision.why: fastest working version that also matches the live-cap requirement (Memory is 'default, capped' per the brief)

decision.question: how does a live LogView redraw when new entries arrive
options: subscribe: push a {write,open,close} object onto logger.outputs, call it on every event
decision.why: outputs already exist as the extension point (Console/JSONL use the same shape); a poll would cost cycles on a page with no new logs and add a timer to clean up
decision.rule: layout#the-layout-never-jumps (no wasted work, no surprise timers)
